title: Record-keeping vocabulary -- what a place may hold, who may write it, how it ages, how much it binds (ADR-015 amendment 8; ADR-019 decision 3)
description: The one home of the words a RECORDS MAP and a CORPUS MAP are written in. The layout declaration (`layout` schema) names every place a host has and the corpus map (`corpus-map` schema) names every place its documents live in; each of their rows says what KIND of truth lives there (`holds`), WHO may write it (`writer`), how it AGES (`lifecycle`) and at most how much a resident may BIND (`authority_ceiling`), and every one of those words is a row of this document -- never an `enum` in a schema and never a list inside an interpreter. A kind also names its PLANE, so a document declares one thing (its kind) and its plane is derived; a plane is never a field on a document and never a directory. The field anchor is records management (ISO 15489: a record has a declared home, an accountable writer and a disposition) read through information architecture. OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION (Cardinal II): this schema constrains the SHAPE of a row, never the set of rows; a new kind, plane, authority, writer or lifecycle is a new row, and no gate that resolves a map against this document is touched.

planes.description: The reading GROUPS a corpus divides into: why one would come to a document at all. A plane is an attribute of a KIND and of nothing else -- it groups kinds, it is projected per plane in the catalog, and it is never written on a document, because a document that named both its kind and its plane could contradict itself.

authorities.description: How much an artifact BINDS -- the single vocabulary for that question, so that no document needs a second `status` field whose values would overlap these (ADR-019 decision 3). Every row carries two machine facts beside its prose, because an interpreter must be able to compare two authorities and to refuse a place that reaches too high WITHOUT holding any of these words in its code (Cardinal IV).

place_default.description: Whether this is the ceiling a place row that declares none is read at. Exactly one row says true, and it is DATA for the same reason the flag beside it is: an interpreter that knew which state was the default would be an interpreter holding the most consequential policy in the vocabulary.

binding_rank.description: How much this state binds, as a comparable number: a declared authority is admitted under a ceiling when its rank is not greater than the ceiling's. Equal ranks bind equally; the number orders the vocabulary and means nothing on its own. This exists so that `above the ceiling` is decidable from data -- an interpreter that knew the order would be an interpreter holding policy.

kinds.description: What a place HOLDS: the kind of truth living there, stated so that a document of another kind found in that place is recognisably misfiled. Every kind names the one plane it belongs to.

plane.description: The id of one `planes` row. Required: a kind with no plane is a document that appears in no section of the catalog, which is how a corpus acquires a part nobody reads.

writers.description: WHO may write a place: an accountable authority, named by what it is accountable FOR, never by a runtime product or a host's role name.

lifecycles.description: How a place's content AGES and where it goes when it is no longer current -- its disposition, in ISO 15489's sense.

criterion_statuses.description: What a card's acceptance criterion may be COMPUTED to be (ADR-020 decision 7). A vocabulary and never an enum in a schema: a new reading of a proof is a row, and no interpreter holds the set. None of these is writable by any principal -- the rows describe results of a resolution, not fields on a document.

appetite_units.description: The units a bet's APPETITE may be declared in (ADR-020 decision 9). The kit ships the words and never a number: how much is the host's, stated on its own card, and a unit is legitimate here only while consumption in it can be read passively from records the system already writes.

transition_modes.description: How a passage between two work states is decided (ADR-020 decision 8). Every transition is one of these or it is an unowned passage, which is how work silently advances; the words live here and the lifecycle grammar carries the parameter each of them needs.
